from_bmlib.title: An undeclared archival master beat the web image beside it
from_bmlib.note: WP 4.1 / 4.5, with bmlib#117. The desktop renders no figure image (`graphic` is in jats_markdown's `_SILENT_TAGS`). Swift ranks a master from `mime-subtype` alone, so an undeclared TIFF deposited first beats the JPEG after it (lite #578). Android keeps the last `<graphic>`, which has no such regression, but its bmlib#117 port must bring this rule with it (lite #165).

from_bmlib.title: A blank `identifier` is no cache key
from_bmlib.note: bmlib `[Unreleased]` after 0.11.0 (bmlib PR #499). Python names the markdown and PDF caches from an unstripped PMC ID, PMID or DOI (`pdf_utils.generate_fulltext_path`, `generate_pdf_path`), so a whitespace-only one is a file shared across documents. Swift's fetch caches refuse a blank id (`ArticleCacheKey.usable()`), but its upload path names the copy `"\(document.pmid).pdf"` (`ScoredDocumentsView.swift`). Android names PDFs by the document's UUID.

from_bmlib.title: `import_retraction_watch_export()`: one export replaces the stored notices
from_bmlib.note: The desktop builds each refresh into a fresh file with `import_retraction_watch_export` (`retraction_export._build`), so an export with no recognised `RetractionNature`, DOI or PMID is refused and the old copy kept; the 1% removal guard is moot over an empty table, and the desktop's 5% shrink guard stands. The apps' retraction plans consume bmlib's Rust through the FFI (#588), so they take this with that pin.
